papers.title: Variational Monte Carlo - Bridging Concepts of Machine Learning and High Dimensional Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: A statistical learning approach for parametric PDEs related to Uncertainty Quantification is derived. The method is based on the minimization of an empirical risk on a selected model class and it is shown to be applicable to a broad range of problems. A general unified convergence analysis is derived, which takes into account the approximation and the statistical errors. By this, a combination of theoretical results from numerical analysis and statistics is obtained. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the method with the model class of hierarchical tensors.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种基于统计学习的参数化PDE求解方法，可应用于不确定性量化，其理论框架和数值方法对生物力学代理模型构建具有潜在迁移价值。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address implant or biomechanics design, lacks constraint handling, and focuses on theoretical convergence analysis rather than practical surrogate modeling for expensive simulations.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决高维参数化PDE的不确定性量化问题
summary_zh.method: 基于经验风险最小化的统计学习方法，结合层次张量模型类
summary_zh.result: 统一收敛性分析结合了数值分析与统计误差，数值实验验证了方法性能
summary_zh.validation: 通过层次张量数值基准实验验证

summary_en.motivation: To develop a statistical learning approach for parametric PDEs that addresses uncertainty quantification in high-dimensional settings.
summary_en.method: The method minimizes empirical risk over a chosen model class, with a unified convergence analysis combining approximation and statistical errors.
summary_en.result: The approach demonstrates applicability to a broad range of problems, with numerical experiments using hierarchical tensors showing effective performance.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed through numerical benchmarks on hierarchical tensor model classes.

papers.title: Sparse Gaussian Process Temporal Difference Learning for Marine Robot Navigation
papers.abstract: We present a method for Temporal Difference (TD) learning that addresses several challenges faced by robots learning to navigate in a marine environment. For improved data efficiency, our method reduces TD updates to Gaussian Process regression. To make predictions amenable to online settings, we introduce a sparse approximation with improved quality over current rejection-based sparse methods. We derive the predictive value function posterior and use the moments to obtain a new algorithm for model-free policy evaluation, SPGP-SARSA. With simple changes, we show SPGP-SARSA can be reduced to a model-based equivalent, SPGP-TD. We perform comprehensive simulation studies and also conduct physical learning trials with an underwater robot. Our results show SPGP-SARSA can outperform the state-of-the-art sparse method, replicate the prediction quality of its exact counterpart, and be applied to solve underwater navigation tasks.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文使用稀疏高斯过程进行时间差分学习，应用于水下机器人导航，与FEA代理建模或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on reinforcement learning for robot navigation, not on surrogate modeling for FEA, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanical implant design.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高水下机器人导航学习的数据效率和在线适用性。
summary_zh.method: 将时间差分学习简化为高斯过程回归，并引入改进的稀疏近似。
summary_zh.result: 所提方法在预测质量和数据效率上优于现有稀疏方法，并成功应用于物理机器人导航。
summary_zh.validation: 通过仿真和真实水下机器人实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve data efficiency and online applicability of temporal difference learning for marine robot navigation.
summary_en.method: Reduces TD learning to Gaussian process regression with a novel sparse approximation that enhances prediction quality.
summary_en.result: The proposed SPGP-SARSA outperforms state-of-the-art sparse methods and matches exact GP performance in navigation tasks.
summary_en.validation: Validated through comprehensive simulations and physical trials with an underwater robot.

papers.title: Semi-supervised and Active-learning Scenarios: Efficient Acoustic Model Refinement for a Low Resource Indian Language
papers.abstract: We address the problem of efficient acoustic-model refinement (continuous retraining) using semi-supervised and active learning for a low resource Indian language, wherein the low resource constraints are having i) a small labeled corpus from which to train a baseline `seed' acoustic model and ii) a large training corpus without orthographic labeling or from which to perform a data selection for manual labeling at low costs. The proposed semi-supervised learning decodes the unlabeled large training corpus using the seed model and through various protocols, selects the decoded utterances with high reliability using confidence levels (that correlate to the WER of the decoded utterances) and iterative bootstrapping. The proposed active learning protocol uses confidence level based metric to select the decoded utterances from the large unlabeled corpus for further labeling. The semi-supervised learning protocols can offer a WER reduction, from a poorly trained seed model, by as much as 50% of the best WER-reduction realizable from the seed model's WER, if the large corpus were labeled and used for acoustic-model training. The active learning protocols allow that only 60% of the entire training corpus be manually labeled, to reach the same performance as the entire data.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究语音识别中的声学模型优化，与有限元代理建模或生物力学设计无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper addresses acoustic model refinement for speech recognition, with no FEA, surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, or biomechanics context.

summary_zh.motivation: 低资源语言声学模型高效优化
summary_zh.method: 半监督与主动学习结合置信度选择
summary_zh.result: 半监督学习可降低50%词错误率
summary_zh.validation: 在语音数据集上对比基线模型

summary_en.motivation: To efficiently refine acoustic models for a low-resource Indian language with limited labeled data.
summary_en.method: Semi-supervised and active learning protocols using confidence-based utterance selection and iterative bootstrapping.
summary_en.result: Semi-supervised learning achieves up to 50% WER reduction relative to the seed model's WER.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on a large unlabeled corpus with WER comparison against fully supervised training.
